text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended Thursday.

LONDON - Stocks set a record as British bonds surged after a drop in British inflation prompted a decision to leave interest rates unchanged. The FTSE 100 index jumped 38.6 points to 4,197.5, its second record of the year.
FRANKFURT - German shares edged higher, with the DAX index rising 4.86 points to a record 2,993.31. In after-hours trading the index stood at 2,996.12.
PARIS - French stocks also set a record and the market remained in a bullish mood despite the Bank of France's inaction on interest rates. The blue-chip CAC-40 index rose 19.79 points to 2,407.77.

ZURICH - Swiss stocks closed firmer with the blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) closing above 4,000 for the first time. The all-share Swiss Performance Index rose 17.10 points to 2,568.85 points and the SMI added 27.5 points to 4,007.1.
TOKYO - Tokyo stocks ended slightly higher after swinging between positive and negative zones. The Nikkei 225 average finished up 51.21 points at 18,144.34.

HONG KONG - The Hang Seng index set another record as investors snatched up stocks left behind in Wednesday's record-breaking rally. The index rose 64.03 points to 13,830.68 in the third busiest session.
SYDNEY - The Australian market ended mixed, with a firmer resources sector failing to overcome a weak industrials. The All Ordinaries index fell 1.9 points to 2,436.3.
JOHANNESBURG - South African shares ended higher after being helped by a firmer gold sector and a bullish short-term outlook for major international markets, dealers said.
The all-share index rose 27.6 points to 6,779, the industrials index jumped 45.7 points to 8,176.4 and the gold index added 12.6 points to 1,421.
